items.q: Adynamic bone disease carries which prognosis?
items.exp: Adynamic bone disease: worst prognosis; bone pain. (Book p812)

items.q: The two causes of adynamic bone disease named are:
opts: Excess calcium supplementation in CKD and aluminum
PTH excess with FGF23 loss in grade 5
Vitamin D excess with magnesium load
items.exp: Cause: excess Ca supplementation in CKD patient; aluminum (aluminium associated bone disease). (Book p812)

items.q: Excess calcium supplementation inhibits PTH to below:
items.exp: Excess Ca supplementation → inhibit PTH (<400 pg). (Book p812)

items.q: The aluminum cause of adynamic bone disease is linked to:
items.exp: Aluminum (aluminium associated bone disease): dialysis dementia. (Book p812)

items.q: In the excess-calcium chain, high Ca⁺ and phosphorus lead to:
opts: Vascular and soft tissue calcification → death
Bone formation with rising PTH levels
items.exp: High Ca⁺ & P phosphorus → vascular and soft tissue calcification → death. (Book p812)

items.q: All but one are the extraskeletal calcification sites shown in the CRF photographs. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Extraskeletal calcification in CRF: arterial, pulmonary, periarticular. (Book p812)

items.q: The treatment of the excess-calcium-driven adynamic state is:
opts: Stop all supplements and dialyze in low calcium dialysate
Increase calcium carbonate with each meal
Start calcitriol daily and add aluminum
Add ferrous sulfate and continue calcium
items.exp: Treatment: stop all supplements; dialysis in low calcium dialysate. (Book p812)

items.q: Dialysis in low calcium dialysate is part of the treatment of adynamic bone disease from excess calcium.
items.exp: Dialysis in low calcium dialysate. (Book p812)

items.q: Match the following drug to its role on this page — 1) Sevelamer carbonate  2) Calcium acetate  3) Cinacalcet  4) Calcitriol … A) CaSR agonist  B) Calcium phosphate binder  C) Pure phosphate binder  D) Active vitamin D
items.exp: Sevelamer (pure binder); calcium acetate (calcium binder); cinacalcet (CaSR agonist); calcitriol (active vitamin D, 0.25 µg alternate days). (Book p812)
